strengths: Does not claim tipping is illegal.
Service charge framed as printed pricing, not folklore percentages.
Consumption-tax vs tip confusion is correctly hedged.
verified: Tipping is not customary in most everyday Japanese restaurants.
Staff often return leftover cash believing it was forgotten change.
Some venues add a printed service charge (sābisu-ryō).
questionable: Many employees are told to return forgotten items and unclear cash promptly.
unsupported: Implied nationwide staff-training curriculum for tip returns.

issues.location: Why Service Is Treated as Included — Staff training paragraph
issues.problem: “Many employees are told…” asserts workplace training content without evidence and reads like a verified institutional fact.
issues.suggestion: Hedge to operational practice: leftover table cash often looks like forgotten change, so staff commonly return it quickly.

issues.problem: No invented percentages, but readers may still want one non-numeric cue for when service charges appear.
issues.suggestion: Keep qualitative triggers (groups, private rooms, luxury) without fabricating rates.
